eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: EL teams polled on whether to ship Glamsterdam with EIP-8037 as is or delay; rough consensus reached to proceed unchanged.

moments.context: Ben Edgington introduced the overhanging ACDE question of whether to commit to shipping EIP-8037 as is or change the spec, with Hoodi targeted for the week of 14 December.

Ansgar polled each EL client team. Geth leaned toward shipping as is since no strong alternative proposal exists; Nethermind said proposals don't move the needle enough; Besu acknowledged its own proposal wasn't strong enough and abstained; Erigon called it the lesser evil; Reth and ethrex explicitly supported shipping as is.
Ansgar summarized that no client unambiguously favored delaying, and asked for any veto. None came; EL rough consensus was reached to lock in Glamsterdam with 8037 unchanged.

eips.summary: Cited in chat as an example of the griefing attacks that full deferral of state gas refills would open up.

moments.context: Toni wrote that fully deferring state gas refills would make users post more gas, opening larger griefing attacks (e.g. 4337, calls to untrusted contracts), and that no spec-change alternative is clearly better than 8037 as implemented.

eips.title: Independent CL/EL Sync
eips.summary: Barnabas suggested CFIing EIP-8237 for Gloas to decouple CL from EL payload syncing, addressing the RLP backfill concern.

moments.context: Barnabas proposed in chat that EIP-8237 (Independent CL/EL Sync) could be CFI'd for Gloas to avoid the CL needing to care about payload syncing and RLP for backfill.

eips.title: Reduce CL Block Retention Window
eips.summary: Barnabas noted EIP-8383 is already CFI'd and will reduce the CL block retention window, lessening the RLP backfill concern.

moments.context: Barnabas pointed out in chat that EIP-8383 is CFI'd to reduce the retention window, so the RLP backfill issue will become even less relevant going forward.

eips.title: Fork-choice enforced Inclusion Lists (FOCIL)
eips.summary: Extensive debate on whether FOCIL should remain an SFI headliner for Hegota or be dropped to prioritize post-quantum work; no decision made, deferred to next call.

moments.context: Ben Edgington proposed reexamining Heze's headliner, EIP-7805 FOCIL, in light of the push to prioritize PQ and AI security, noting that removing a headliner would be an extraordinary decision for which he'd want near-unanimity from client teams, including EL teams.

Thomas (soispoke) laid out options: no FOCIL, FOCIL V0 without frames support, minimal FOCIL plus frames with no aggregation (the preferred path), and full PQ FOCIL with aggregation. The argument was that a Hegota cut to FOCIL and frames need not materially delay PQCL.
Jihoon argued FOCIL is in late development and can be pipelined alongside PQ research, with limited impact on PQ timelines, since researchers and developers have different skill sets.
Andrew Ashikhmin argued FOCIL does not solve censorship in full blocks and is far from finished, making it a massive distraction from PQ work.
Caspar argued FOCIL should be dropped because Hegota should be reprioritized to include only PQ-critical items, and FOCIL competes for the same bottleneck of high-context people.

Ben Adams said FOCIL's spec is now incomplete due to PQ unknowns, putting it at risk, but killing it now might be premature. Fabio from Besu supported keeping a bare minimum FOCIL. Lodestar said FOCIL is already implemented on CL and doesn't see the overlap. Ivan from ethrex was undecided.
Ben Edgington drew a line, stating the decision on FOCIL and full Heze scope will be made on the next call in two weeks.

eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation
eips.summary: Referenced as a potential approach for in-mempool signature and proof aggregation and its interaction with FOCIL and PQ transactions.

moments.context: Thomas noted that if Hegota does not include 8288-style mempool aggregation, FOCIL works out of the box with PQ transactions without spec changes, since each IL just holds fewer PQ transactions.
Felix suggested in chat that EIP-8288 has structural similarities to FOCIL networking needs and could be another avenue to ship FOCIL, avoiding relaying large PQ transaction bundles in the CL.

eips.title: Set Code for EOAs
eips.summary: Thomas mentioned 7702 transactions as one of the legacy types that a minimal FOCIL version without frames support could still include.

moments.context: Thomas listed legacy transactions and 7702 as the transaction types a FOCIL V0 (without frames support) would be limited to including in inclusion lists.

eips.title: Fee market change for ETH 1.0 chain
eips.summary: Raised in chat as the answer to the full-block censorship argument against FOCIL: base fees keep rising, so the attack cannot be sustained.

moments.context: Replying in chat to Andrew's point that a builder can fill blocks to bypass FOCIL, Thomas said the attack can't be sustained because base fees keep going up; Marius replied '1559???', which Thomas thumbed up.

eips.title: Uniform price auction over inclusion lists
eips.summary: Anders referenced EIP-8046 as a complement to FOCIL for solving censorship resistance in full blocks.

moments.context: Anders posted in chat that EIP-8046 (Uniform Price Auction over Inclusion Lists, UPIL) exists on top of FOCIL to address censorship resistance in full blocks, but noted it is probably a later discussion.
